fields.reasoning: No change set ever reaches the ready trigger with request_kind milestone: a milestone request's plan run opens a record change set, which lands straight from in-flight and is never accepted-and-ready (changeset fold.go:606, lifecycle.go:160; request-trigger-dispatch keeps that), and change sets a milestone plan or rhiza change new opens get request_kind feature (change-set-records-dispatch, dispatch-kind-field-request-kind). A [ready] milestone rule would pass rhiza check yet never fire, which is the silent no-op the plan otherwise refuses (unknown keys are errors, unresolved workflows are attention). Dropping the key is the smaller change and keeps the file honest; inventing a path that gives a ready change set kind milestone would add lifecycle behaviour the intent never asked for. If such a path is added later, the key can be admitted then.
fields.statement: The [ready] table in .rhiza/dispatch.toml accepts only the kinds feature and bug; a milestone key under [ready] is an error naming it, like any other unknown key, and rhiza check reports it. [request] keeps all three kinds (feature, bug, milestone). This narrows workflow-dispatch-rules-file and dispatch-rules-file: 'each maps a kind (feature, bug, milestone)' holds for [request] only, and the ready resolver never looks up a milestone rule.
